sentences.text: Averianov and colleagues revised the estimated size of Ulughbegsaurus to approximately 7.4 meters based on a new overlapping specimen.
The animal is estimated to have had a body length between 7.5 and 8 meters and a weight of more than 1000 kilograms.
The holotype specimen, which is the specific example the species is based on, has a preserved length of 242 millimeters.
The maxilla bone is triangular in lateral view and touches the nasal fossa.
This maxilla bone has at least eight teeth.
The lower outer side of the maxilla bone features a series of shallow oval depressions.
The anterior ramus of the maxilla appears to have a vertical biting edge, unlike the backward-sloping edge typical of carcharodontosaurids.
The maxilla shows at least six vertical crests between the second and seventh tooth.
The high frontal rampart protruding from the interdental plates has a series of four large vein channels extending along the top.
The inner side of the posterior ramus contribution to the window has pneumatic recesses projecting forward and downward into the bone.
Due to its size, Ulughbegsaurus may have been the apex predator of its ecosystem.
Fossil material of Ulughbegsaurus was discovered in the Bissekty Formation, Uzbekistan, during the 1980s.
Tanaka and colleagues formally described the genus and species Ulughbegsaurus uzbekistanensis in 2021.
In 2025, Averianov et al. assigned a right maxilla fragment from the early Cenomanian Khodzhakul Formation of Uzbekistan to Ulughbegsaurus sp.
A partial Acrocanthosaurus-like posterior dorsal vertebra found in the Bissekty Formation in 2024 may belong to Ulughbegsaurus.
There are three recorded fossil occurrences of Ulughbegsaurus.
Ulughbegsaurus coexisted with other carnivorous theropods in the environment of the Bissekty Formation.
Contemporaneous carnivores included the tyrannosauroid Timurlengia and the dromaeosaurid Itemirus.
The teeth of Ulughbegsaurus are notably narrower than those of Timurlengia.
This suggests that carcharodontosaurids remained the dominant carnivorous theropods over tyrannosauroids as late as the Turonian, at least in Asia.
Researchers later confirmed that Ulughbegsaurus is a valid carcharodontosaurian taxon after discovering a second comparable maxilla fragment.
Based on shared characters with Carcharodontosaurus, Ulughbegsaurus is most likely referred to the family Carcharodontosauridae.
Tanaka et al. used two different phylogenetic datasets to determine the relationships of Ulughbegsaurus.
One phylogenetic analysis placed Ulughbegsaurus in a polytomy including Neovenator and megaraptorans.
A second analysis placed Ulughbegsaurus in a polytomy with other basal carcharodontosaurids.
Ulughbegsaurus lived during the Turonian stage, between 93.9 and 89.8 million years ago.
A 2022 study debated whether Ulughbegsaurus was a nomen dubium lacking diagnostic features and possibly originated from a dromaeosaurid.
A 2022 study suggested that Ulughbegsaurus is a nomen dubium due to a lack of diagnostic features.
Researchers suggested it was plausible that the jaw fragment originated from a dromaeosaurid.
